nodes.title: Ise: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Ise. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: An enterprise is deploying Cisco ISE 3.x in a distributed architecture with two ?
flashcards.back: In ISE, only the primary PAN is writeable. The secondary PAN receives replicated configuration and becomes writeable only after a failover (manual, or auto-failover if configured). PSNs handle RADIUS/authentication, not PANs, and PSNs cannot be auto-promoted to PAN. the secondary PAN is a warm standby promoted manually or via auto-failover

flashcards.front: An engineer must enforce posture compliance so that only laptops with up-to-date?
flashcards.back: The ISE Posture Module (inside AnyConnect/Secure Client) evaluates the endpoint against posture policies. Non-compliant devices are given a restricted dACL and URL redirect to a remediation portal (patch server, AV update). Profiling identifies devices, it does not remediate them.

flashcards.front: A Cisco ISE administrator wants non-compliant devices to be automatically quaran?
flashcards.back: RFC 5176 RADIUS CoA lets ISE push a reauthentication or session termination to the NAS in real time. ISE uses this to dynamically enforce policy changes, such as moving a posture-violating endpoint into a restricted VLAN/dACL and back when remediated.

flashcards.front: A company wants to allow contractors temporary wireless access via a self-regist?
flashcards.back: The ISE Self-Registered Guest Portal lets visitors create an account, optionally approved by a sponsor, and delivers credentials via email/SMS. The BYOD, Posture, and MyDevices portals serve different purposes (certificate provisioning, compliance checking, device lifecycle).

nodes.title: Network Security: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Network Security. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: An engineer is hardening the control plane of a core Cisco IOS-XE router. Traffi?
flashcards.back: CoPP classifies traffic punted to the route processor into policy classes (routing, management, monitoring, undesirable) and applies rate-limiters so that floods of any single class cannot starve legitimate control-plane traffic. uRPF addresses source spoofing, ACLs do not rate-limit, and Storm Control is a Layer 2 feature on data-plane interfaces.

flashcards.front: A security architect wants to prevent rogue DHCP servers on an access switch and?
flashcards.back: DHCP snooping builds a binding table of legitimate IP-to-MAC-to-port mappings and blocks DHCP server responses on untrusted ports. DAI then validates ARP packets against that binding table, dropping gratuitous ARP spoofs. IP Source Guard complements this by filtering data traffic, but DAI is the specific ARP inspection feature. plus Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) referencing the snooping binding table

flashcards.front: A penetration tester gains access to a VLAN through a vulnerable kiosk and sends?
flashcards.back: Double-tagging attacks work when the native VLAN on a trunk is used by normal access ports and when DTP allows unsolicited trunk negotiation. Hardcoding access ports, disabling DTP, using a dedicated unused native VLAN, and tagging it with vlan dot1q tag native prevent the attack. plus assign a dedicated unused native VLAN on trunks and tag native VLANs

flashcards.front: An engineer configures OSPF authentication between two Cisco routers. The securi?
flashcards.back: Modern IOS/IOS-XE supports HMAC-SHA cryptographic authentication for OSPF using key chains with rotation and lifetimes. Legacy MD5 is still available but weaker. BGP-style neighbor password and null authentication are unrelated.

nodes.title: Vpn: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Vpn. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A financial services company is designing an IPsec site-to-site VPN between two ?
flashcards.back: PFS is achieved by performing a fresh Diffie-Hellman exchange during each IPsec SA rekey. Configuring a DH group in the IPsec proposal (Phase 2) forces that new exchange, so even if long-term keys are later compromised, previously recorded sessions cannot be decrypted. Stronger ciphers, short lifetimes, and DPD do not by themselves guarantee PFS.

flashcards.front: An engineer troubleshoots an IKEv2 site-to-site VPN stuck in MM_WAIT_MSG2. Both ?
flashcards.back: MM_WAIT_MSG2 in the phase-1 state machine means the initiator is waiting for the first response from the peer. The overwhelming cause is Layer 3/4: UDP 500 (or 4500 with NAT-T) is dropped by a firewall or NAT without NAT-T. Proposal, PSK, and ACL mismatches appear in later states.

flashcards.front: An engineer configures Cisco AnyConnect (Secure Client) remote access VPN on an ?
flashcards.back: Split tunneling with an include ACL (tunnelspecified) pushes only the listed subnets down the VPN, while everything else uses the client's local Internet. Hair-pinning is used for client-to-client traffic through the same ASA interface, not for Internet offload.

flashcards.front: An architect is choosing between Cisco DMVPN and GETVPN for a large multi-site M?
flashcards.back: GETVPN uses group keys distributed by a Key Server via GDOI. Because it does not tunnel-encapsulate, the original IP header is preserved, which lets MPLS routing and multicast work natively across the encrypted overlay. DMVPN/FlexVPN tunnel the traffic, changing outer headers.

nodes.title: Cloud Security: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Cloud Security. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A healthcare company stores PHI in an AWS S3 bucket. They must ensure data is en?
flashcards.back: SSE-KMS with a customer-managed CMK gives the customer control over key policy, rotation, and audit via CloudTrail. Combining it with an IAM role and a bucket policy referencing the role ARN ensures only authorized identities can decrypt. Public access contradicts PHI protection; hard-coded static keys are bad practice.

flashcards.front: A CIO is evaluating Cisco Secure Workload (Tetration). Which primary security be?
flashcards.back: Secure Workload collects telemetry from agents on every workload, discovers application dependencies, then generates and enforces microsegmentation policies (allow-list) at the host level. It works identically on bare metal, VMs, containers, AWS, Azure, and GCP. It is not a WAN optimizer or DDoS scrubber.

flashcards.front: A CASB product (Cisco Cloudlock) flags that several employees uploaded sensitive?
flashcards.back: CASBs inspect SaaS activity via API and inline modes: they discover Shadow IT, classify data (DLP), and apply policy against unsanctioned or risky sharing. Cloudlock integrates with Salesforce, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, etc. It is not a DNS or K8s tool.

flashcards.front: Which statement about Zero Trust Architecture is accurate?
flashcards.back: NIST SP 800-207 defines Zero Trust around three tenets: verify explicitly (identity, device, context), use least-privileged access, and assume breach. Network location is not a trust anchor, and encryption remains essential. continuously verifies every access request, and enforces least privilege regardless of network location

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: An engineer observes that a Cisco Secure Firewall (FTD) managed by FMC is blocki?
flashcards.back: Pinned applications reject any certificate not matching the exact pinned copy, so Decrypt-Resign breaks them. The supported approach is to add a Do Not Decrypt rule for the specific destination (URL category, SNI, or application) while keeping decryption enabled globally. Importing a private key is not possible (you do not own the partner's), and disabling the SSL policy is too broad.

flashcards.front: A developer integrates a third-party application with Cisco FMC using the REST A?
flashcards.back: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests indicates rate limiting. FMC caps REST API calls (typically 120 messages per minute per client/IP). Reducing polling frequency, using subscription-based mechanisms, or spacing calls fixes the issue. Expired tokens return 401, missing headers return 415.

flashcards.front: An engineer is configuring a Cisco Secure Firewall access control policy. A rule?
flashcards.back: The Allow action passes traffic through the AC rule while letting attached inspection (intrusion, file, variable set) run on it. Trust bypasses inspection. Monitor is passive and cannot be terminal. Block prevents traffic entirely.

flashcards.front: A Snort 3 rule on Cisco Secure Firewall uses the option http_uri; content:"admin?
flashcards.back: Snort 3 introduced buffers (http_uri, http_header, http_client_body, etc.) that isolate where content matching is applied. http_uri limits the match to the normalized request URI, preventing false positives from payload elsewhere.
